values.claude: Passport valid for at least 6 months beyond entry recommended
values.deepseek: Valid for at least 6 months beyond entry date
values.gemini: 6 months beyond date of entry
values.grok: At least 6 months beyond your planned stay in Morocco

values.claude: Return/onward ticket may be requested at check-in or entry
values.gemini: Yes
values.grok: Proof of onward or return travel is often requested

values.claude: Keep a copy of your passport; carry ID as police checkpoints exist, especially near the Sahara.
values.deepseek: Blank page required for entry stamp.
values.gemini: Ensure passport has at least one blank page for entry stamp.
values.grok: One blank passport page required for entry stamp. Proof of sufficient funds may be requested.

values.claude: Cash-heavy economy. Cards accepted at hotels, larger restaurants, and modern shops in cities; souks, taxis, small cafes, and rural areas are cash-only.
values.deepseek: Cash is king, especially in medinas, souks, small restaurants, and for taxis. Cards accepted at hotels, upscale restaurants, and large supermarkets.
values.gemini: Cash is king; cards accepted in large hotels/high-end riads/modern shops.
values.grok: Cash (MAD) is king in souks and smaller places; cards accepted in tourist areas, hotels, and larger restaurants. ATMs widely available at airports and cities.

values.claude: ATMs widespread in cities and towns; withdraw dirham on arrival (airport ATMs work). Sparse in the deep Sahara — carry cash for desert legs.
values.deepseek: Widely available in cities and at airports. Use major banks (BMCE, Banque Populaire, Crédit Agricole). Withdrawal limits vary.
values.gemini: Widespread in cities, rare in remote areas/desert.
values.grok: Good in cities and tourist areas; withdraw MAD on arrival at CMN or RAK airports.

values.claude: Dirham is a closed/non-convertible currency: importing or exporting it is restricted/prohibited. Convert leftover dirham back to USD/EUR before departing (keep ATM/exchange receipts).
values.deepseek: No limit on foreign currency import, but amounts over MAD 100,000 must be declared. Export of MAD is restricted.
values.gemini: 1000 MAD limit on export; declare large amounts of foreign currency upon entry.
values.grok: Declare amounts over 100,000 MAD or equivalent $10,000 USD

values.claude: Tipping expected but modest: round up taxis, ~10% in restaurants if no service charge, small tips (a few dirham) for porters, guides, gas attendants, and hammam staff.
values.deepseek: 5-10% at restaurants if service not included; 20-50 MAD for guides; 10-20 MAD for porters.
values.gemini: 10% in restaurants, small change for service/bags, round up for taxis.
values.grok: 10-15% in restaurants for good service; small tips (5-10 MAD) for guides, porters, and taxi drivers common.

values.deepseek: Royal Air Maroc
values.gemini: Royal Air Maroc
values.grok: Royal Air Maroc (RAM)

values.claude: ONCF trains connect Casablanca, Rabat, Fez, Marrakech, Tangier; comfortable and punctual. Al Boraq high-speed line runs Tangier–Casablanca. Book first class for reserved seats. Note: NO train to Chefchaouen, Essaouira, or the Sahara.
values.deepseek: ONCF operates trains including the high-speed Al Boraq (Tangier-Casablanca) and conventional lines connecting major cities.
values.gemini: ONCF network is efficient, safe, and cost-effective (Casa, Rabat, Fez, Marrakech).
values.grok: ONCF trains are reliable, comfortable, and affordable between major cities like Casablanca, Marrakech, Fez.

values.claude: CTM and Supratours are the reliable intercity coach companies — used to reach Chefchaouen, Essaouira, and Sahara gateways not on the rail network. Book ahead in high season.
values.deepseek: CTM and Supratours are the main intercity bus companies, offering comfortable and reliable service.
values.gemini: Supratours and CTM are the most reliable and comfortable for Americans.
values.grok: CTM and Supratours buses are good options for smaller towns and budget travel.

values.claude: Royal Air Maroc and low-cost carriers link major cities; usually unnecessary for the compact first-timer loop.
values.deepseek: Royal Air Maroc operates domestic routes, including Casablanca to major cities.
values.gemini: Available, usually through Royal Air Maroc.
values.grok: RAM and others connect major cities affordably.

values.claude: Petit taxis (metered, in-city) and grand taxis (shared, intercity) are standard. Careem operates in some cities; insist on the meter or agree fare first in petit taxis.
values.deepseek: Apps like Careem, Heetch, and InDrive operate in some cities. BlaBlaCar for intercity ridesharing.
values.gemini: Limited to specific apps in large cities (e.g., inDrive, Roby).
values.grok: Careem (Uber-like) available in major cities; grand taxis and petit taxis common.

values.claude: Drive on the RIGHT. US license accepted for short stays (IDP recommended). Cities are chaotic and parking is hard; many first-timers hire a driver instead. Toll motorways connect major cities. Police checkpoints common; keep documents handy.
values.deepseek: Valid US driver's license accepted; IDP recommended. Drive on the right. Rental companies require credit card and passport.
values.gemini: Driving is intense in cities; recommended only for experienced drivers on motorways or rural roads. International Driving Permit recommended.
values.grok: Drive on the right; International Driving Permit recommended with US license. Roads vary; cautious driving advised due to local habits.

values.claude: Spring (Mar–May) and fall (Sep–Nov) are ideal: warm days, cool nights. Summer (Jun–Aug) is very hot inland (Marrakech, Fez, Sahara can exceed 100°F/38°C); coast (Essaouira) stays mild. Winter (Dec–Feb) is cool, Atlas gets snow, desert nights are cold.
values.deepseek: Mediterranean along coast, continental inland, desert in south. Spring (Mar-May) and Fall (Sep-Nov) are mild. Summer (Jun-Aug) is hot inland. Winter (Dec-Feb) is cool with snow in Atlas.
values.gemini: Spring (Mar-May) and Autumn (Sep-Nov) are mild. Summer is very hot, especially inland/desert. Winter is mild but nights are cold.
values.grok: Spring (Mar-May) and Fall (Sep-Nov): mild 60-80°F (15-27°C). Summer hot (esp. inland >100°F/38°C). Winter mild coast, cold mountains/desert nights.

values.claude: US State Dept typically 'Level 2: Exercise Increased Caution' (terrorism) — VERIFY current level and date before travel.
values.deepseek: Level 2: Exercise Increased Caution
values.gemini: Level 2 (Exercise Increased Caution) - US Department of State (check current status)
values.grok: Level 2: Exercise Increased Caution (due to terrorism) as of April 2025

values.claude: Petty crime (pickpocketing, aggressive touts/faux guides, medina scams) far more likely than violent crime. Morocco is generally considered safe for tourists including solo travelers with normal precautions.
values.deepseek: Petty crime, scams, and overzealous attention in tourist areas.
values.gemini: Petty theft, street harassment (touts), traffic accidents.
values.grok: Petty crime, scams in tourist areas, road safety, terrorism in some areas

values.claude: No mandatory vaccines for US travelers from the US; routine vaccinations up to date; Hep A and typhoid commonly recommended for food/water exposure — consult a travel clinic.
values.deepseek: Routine vaccines (MMR, DTP, varicella, flu) recommended. Hepatitis A and Typhoid recommended for most travelers.
values.gemini: Routine vaccines, Hepatitis A/B recommended. Consult CDC.
values.grok: Routine vaccines recommended; hepatitis A, typhoid advised for most travelers. No mandatory.

values.claude: Stick to bottled or filtered water; tap water is chlorinated in cities but often causes stomach upset for visitors. Avoid ice from unknown sources.
values.deepseek: Officially safe in major cities, but not recommended for tourists due to potential stomach upset. Stick to bottled water.
values.gemini: Bottled water recommended for drinking.
values.grok: Not recommended; stick to bottled water.

values.claude: Local SIMs (Maroc Telecom, Orange, Inwi) cheap with data-heavy tourist packages, sold at airports/shops (passport needed). eSIMs (Airalo etc.) let you land connected — good since the dirham is closed and you may want maps/rideshare immediately on arrival.
values.deepseek: Local SIMs available at airports (Orange, Maroc Telecom, Inwi). eSIMs (Airalo, Ubigi) can be activated before arrival.
values.gemini: Maroc Telecom, Orange, Inwi. eSIMs (Airalo, etc.) are easy for US travelers.
values.grok: eSIMs and local SIMs (Maroc Telecom, Orange, Inwi) easy at airports. Good for Americans with unlocked phones.

values.claude: Strong 4G/5G in cities and along main routes; patchy to none in the deep Sahara and remote Atlas — download offline maps before desert legs.
values.deepseek: Good 4G/5G coverage in cities and major towns; spotty in rural/desert areas.
values.gemini: Excellent in cities/towns; spotty in deep Sahara/Atlas Mountains.
values.grok: Strong in cities and tourist routes; spotty in remote desert/mountains.

values.claude: Morocco is a Muslim country; dress modestly especially outside tourist zones — shoulders and knees covered is respectful. Women aren't required to cover hair (except inside some religious sites, most of which are closed to non-Muslims). Cities like Marrakech are used to tourists; rural areas are more conservative. Lightweight, covering clothing also helps with sun and heat.
values.deepseek: Modest dress appreciated. Cover shoulders and knees, especially in medinas and rural areas.
values.gemini: Modest clothing recommended; shoulders and knees covered, especially in rural areas or religious sites.
values.grok: Modest clothing recommended, especially for women in medinas and rural areas. Cover shoulders and knees at religious sites. Lightweight, breathable fabrics for heat.

claude: Do use your right hand for eating and greeting
Do ask before photographing people (especially women and vendors)
Don't enter mosques unless signed open to non-Muslims (most aren't)
Do remove shoes when entering homes/riads where indicated
Don't show public displays of affection
Do accept mint tea when offered — it's hospitality
Be discreet with alcohol — legal for tourists but not consumed publicly
deepseek: Don't eat with your left hand
Don't take photos of people without permission
gemini: Do not photograph people without permission
